Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 15.02.2012 passed in MVC.No.151/2008 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and A.M.A.C.T-7, Shimoga, (in short, 'the Tribunal').
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are, on 25.12.2005, while the petitioner was traveling in the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-14/R-5325 as pillion rider, ridded by his brother, Ravikumar, near Jayapadma and Nandihalli cross, at about 11.30 a.m., a Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-02/N-7671, which was driven by respondent No.2 from the opposite direction hit against the motor cycle and caused injuries to the petitioner.
He was treated at Government Hospital, Shikaripura, Nanjappa Hospital, Shimoga Sri S M Vijaykymar vs Pradesh Janata Dal on 14 August, 2024

2 and KMC Manipal Hospital, under hospitalization for 57 days.
Thereafter, he has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.9,80,000/-.
Respondent Nos.1 to 3 have opposed the claim.

The Tribunal, after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties by the impugned judgment allowed the claim petition granting compensation of Rs.4,34,000/- with interest at 6%
p.a. directed the driver of the jeep-respondent No.4 to pay the compensation and dismissed the claim against respondent Nos.1 to 3.
Pleading inadequacy, seeking NC: 2024:KHC:32875 enhancement and also questioning the dismissal of the claim against respondent Nos.1 to 3, the petitioner is before this Court on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri Rameshchandra, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Respondent Nos.1, 3 and 4 are served and remained absent.
Respondent No.2 though appeared though his advocate, remained absent.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered multiple fractures of right femur, left clavicle and right greater toe.
He was treated under hospitalization for 57 days and more than Rs.1,69,000/- has been spent towards treatment.
The petitioner was working as a Government servant now he retired from the service.
The Tribunal did not properly assess the compensation and sought for enhancement.
It is further contended that the Tribunal has erroneously dismissed the claim against respondent Nos.1 to 3.

Respondent No.1 is the Pradesh Janatha Dal, it was taken over as Janatha Dal Secular and the Tribunal did not consider these aspects and made a guess work that Pradesh Janatha Dal is not in existence and has erroneously dismissed the claim against respondent Nos.1 to 3.
6.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by learned counsel for the petitioner also perused the materials on record.
7. It is contended that the Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-02/N-7671 is belonging to Pradesh Janatha Dal.
The 'B' extract of the Jeep is made available as Ex.P1.
On perusal of the same, it is pertinent to note that the Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-02/N-7671 stands in the name of President, Karnataka Pradesh Janatha Dal, No.3, Race Course Road, Bengaluru.
The date of registration of the vehicle was on 07.05.1999.
The NC: 2024:KHC:32875 prosecution papers are also made available, wherein it is alleged that the said vehicle belonging to Janatha Dal.
Ex.P2 is the Police Notice points out that only the vehicle details and the driver details, it did not point out who is the owner of the Jeep.

When the petitioner has placed the material issued by the authoritative department that the owner of the vehicle in question is President, Pradesh Janatha Dal, there is no need to go in detail about the ownership of the vehicle.

8. In connection with the dispute between the Janatha Dal and the Karnataka Pradesh Congress in respect of the Building No.3, Race Course Road, Bengaluru, a civil litigation has been decided by the Division Bench of this Court in Janatha Dal Party, Bengaluru Vs. The Indian National Congress and Others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
At paras 30, 64, 74, 92, 94 and 95, there is detailed discussion that Janatha Dal Secular (Janatha Dal (S)) is the one which taken over the Janatha Dal after its division as Janatha Dal (S)
Sri S M Vijaykymar vs Pradesh Janata Dal on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34416865/
3 and Janata Dal (U).

entities.text: Sri S M Vijaykymar vs Pradesh Janata Dal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court had directed the Janatha Dal (S) to deliver the said building to Karnataka Pradesh Congress Party.

From it is very clear that Janatha Dal (S) is the successor of the Janatha Dal and therefore, the Tribunal has committed error in holding that the Janatha Dal (S)
cannot be held as successor of Pradesh Janatha Dal.
9.
The Tribunal has also committed error in directing the petitioner to recover compensation from 4th respondent alone who was the driver.
Respondent No.2 was the Ex-President and respondent No.3 was the in-charge of Janatha Dal, Shivmoga at relevant point of time and they are the formal parties.
Janatha Dal (S) is the real representative of 1st respondent.
In a claim arising out of this nature, there is a liability on the part of the owner and the driver to pay the compensation to the victim of an accident.

Hence, respondent Nos.1 and 4 are jointly and severally liable NC:
2024:KHC:32875 to pay the compensation that has been assessed in this case.

10. As regarding the assessment of compensation is concerned, the wound certificate points out that the petitioner has suffered fracture of right femur-subtrochantric, segmental fracture of shaft right side, un-displaced fracture clavicle lateral end left side, un-displaced fracture distal phalanx of right great toe.
He was treated at Government hospital, Shikaripura, Nanjappa hospital, Shivamogga and KMC Manipal Hospital, under hospitalization for 57 days.
Medical bills produced before the Tribunal is more than Rs.1,70,000/- wherein the Tribunal has considered a sum of Rs.1,69,000/-.

The petitioner has traveled to Shikaripura, Shivamogga and Mangalore and the Tribunal has assessed Rs.30,000/- towards incidental charges, towards loss of amenities and discomfort at Rs.50,000/-, towards pain and suffering at Rs.1,00,000/-, towards future treatment at NC:
2024:KHC:32875 Rs.25,000/-, towards loss of income during laid up at Rs.30,000/- and towards food and nourishment and attendant charges at Rs.30,000/-, in all Rs.4,34,000/- the same is fair just and proper.

11. At the time of accident, the petitioner was a Government servant and he has continued the service even after the accident and there is no question of awarding any compensation towards loss of future income on account of the disability.
12. The accident is of the year 2005, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation liberally and it is not a case for enhancement.
Hence, the appeal filed by the petitioner merits consideration only to the extent of liability.
